nursing.title: Nursing at home
nursing.lead: Registered nurses and registered practical nurses providing clinical care at home, within the scope of practice set by their regulatory college.
nursing.section1Body: People who need clinical care — wound care, medication administration, catheter or ostomy support, or monitoring after a hospital stay — and would rather receive it at home than in a facility.
nursing.section2Body: We coordinate with your physician, hospital discharge planner or community care team, keep one consistent point of contact, and tell families what changed after every visit.
nursing.section3Body: Nursing is regulated care. Registered nurses and registered practical nurses hold a licence with their provincial college and perform controlled acts that personal support workers and companions cannot.

dementia.title: Dementia support at home
dementia.lead: Support built around what is still familiar — the same faces, the same routine, and a home that does not have to change.
dementia.section1Body: A care plan starts from the person's own history, language, faith and daily rhythm, because familiarity does more for someone living with dementia than any new routine we could introduce.
dementia.section2Body: You get the same small group of caregivers rather than whoever is available, a note after each visit, and a care coordinator who answers the phone.
dementia.section3Body: We describe people by what they can still do. Caregivers are trained to redirect rather than correct, and never to argue with a memory.

aboutPage.title: Rooted in respect, built for Canadian families
aboutPage.lead: Jarkabi Home Care began in Ottawa with one idea: care should fit the person, not the schedule.
aboutPage.differenceLead: Our team of registered nurses and skilled caregivers provide coordinated home care to help families manage recovery, ageing and daily life at home.
aboutPage.differenceBody: We are a home care organisation built around the person — not a staffing agency rotating unfamiliar faces. The safety and wellbeing of every client comes first in how we match caregivers, write plans and communicate with families.
aboutPage.storyBody: Jarkabi Home Care was founded for families who wanted something better than a rota of unfamiliar faces. We started with a small team and a rule we still keep — the same caregivers, every visit, for as long as the family wants them. The organisation is built to serve more Canadian communities over time, but only where we can staff them to the same standard.
aboutPage.missionLead: Everything we do is driven by one aim: to help people live safely, independently and with dignity at home.
aboutPage.missionBody: When Jarkabi began, the goal was simple — care that fits the person, not a schedule on a wall. That vision still guides every plan we write and every caregiver we match.
visionPoints: Care that respects how someone has always lived at home.
Hope and practical support for the whole family — not just the person receiving care.
aboutPage.visionBody: A Canadian home-care organisation that combines local heart with national capability, cultural responsiveness and clinical professionalism.
aboutPage.healthcareTitle: How do home care and nursing support work together?
aboutPage.healthcareBody: We often work alongside nurses, therapists and family doctors. When a prescription changes or a therapist sets a new routine, our caregivers are in the home day after day to help your loved one follow that plan safely and consistently.
aboutPage.healthcareCallout: If you or a loved one needs support at home, we encourage you to reach out for a complimentary conversation so we can suggest an appropriate plan of care.
aboutPage.valuesSubtitle: Six commitments that shape how every care plan is written and every visit is staffed.

values.title: Dignity first
values.body: Care is delivered the way the person would do it themselves, at their pace, with their preferences respected.

values.title: Continuity of caregiver
values.body: The same small group of caregivers wherever possible. Families tell us this matters more than anything else.

values.title: Cultural and linguistic respect
values.body: Food, faith, holidays and language are part of the care plan rather than an afterthought.

values.title: Honest scope
values.body: We say plainly what we can and cannot do, and we never imply service in a community we do not yet serve.

values.title: Family communication
values.body: A note after each visit and a coordinator who answers the phone — including for families living out of province.

values.title: Professional oversight
values.body: Caregivers escalate concerns to a coordinator, not to the family, and health-related plans are reviewed by a nurse.

aboutPage.leadershipBody: Our care team is led by a clinical director and a care director, supported by coordinators who know every client by name. Named profiles are published as the team grows.

whyPage.title: Care built on trust, compassion, and professional standards
whyPage.lead: Twelve things families ask about before choosing a home care provider, answered plainly.
whyPage.introTitle: Why families choose Jarkabi Home Care
whyPage.introBody: Home care should feel personal, professional, and predictable. Jarkabi combines licensed caregivers, nurse-reviewed plans, and coordinators who stay reachable — so dignity stays at the centre of every visit.

items.title: Care that starts with listening
items.body: The first conversation is not a sales call. We ask what a good day looks like, what has already been tried, and what the family is worried about.

items.title: Personalized care planning
items.body: Every plan is written for one person — their routine, their health needs, their language, their household. Nothing is copied from a template.

items.title: A professional care team
items.body: Personal support workers, health care aides, companions and nurses, each working within their own scope of practice.

items.title: Caregiver matching
items.body: We match on skill first, then on personality, language and culture, because a good fit is what makes care feel like help rather than intrusion.

items.title: Clinical oversight
items.body: Plans involving health needs are reviewed by a nurse, and caregivers raise concerns with a coordinator rather than leaving them with the family.

items.title: Dependable scheduling
items.body: From a few hours a week to around-the-clock cover. If a caregiver cannot attend, you hear from us before the visit, not after it.

items.title: Continuity of care
items.body: We protect the caregiver relationship. Changing the person who walks through the door is the last thing we do, not the first.

items.title: Family communication
items.body: A note after each visit, a coordinator who picks up, and a shared view of the care plan for everyone who needs it.

items.title: Respect for culture
items.body: Meals, observances and household customs belong in the care plan. We ask about them at the assessment rather than waiting to get it wrong.

items.title: Respect for language
items.body: We match caregivers by language wherever we can, and this site is published in seven, including Tigrinya, Blin, Tigre, Arabic and Amharic.

items.title: Flexible support
items.body: Needs change after a fall, a discharge or a diagnosis. The plan and the hours change with them, without renegotiating a contract.

items.title: Quality improvement
items.body: We ask for feedback, record it and act on it. A complaint reaches a coordinator the same day it is made.

caregiversPage.title: People who bring skill, respect and warmth into the home
caregiversPage.lead: Who our caregivers are, how they are screened, and how we decide who comes to your door.

sections.title: Who our caregivers are
sections.body: Personal support workers, health care aides, companions, registered practical nurses and registered nurses. Each works within their own scope of practice, and we tell you which role is attending before the first visit.

sections.title: Screening and training
sections.body: Every caregiver completes an interview, reference checks and a criminal record check with vulnerable sector screening before their first shift. Credentials are verified against the issuing college or training provider, and orientation covers infection control, safe transfers and reporting.

sections.title: How we match caregivers
sections.body: Skill comes first: the caregiver has to be able to do what the care plan asks. After that we match on language, culture, personality and schedule, and we ask the family after the first week whether the fit is right.

sections.title: Supervision and support
sections.body: Caregivers report to a coordinator, not to the family. Concerns about a change in health, a fall or a missed medication are escalated the same day, and care plans involving health needs are reviewed by a nurse.

howCareWorksPage.communicationBody: You receive a note after each visit covering what was done, how the day went and anything that changed. A coordinator is reachable during business hours, and families living outside the province get the same updates as those next door.
howCareWorksPage.supervisionBody: Caregivers escalate concerns to a coordinator rather than leaving them with the family. Care plans are reviewed on a regular schedule and immediately after any hospital stay, fall or change in medication.

legalPages.privacyLead: How Jarkabi Home Care collects, uses and protects personal information.
legalPages.privacyBody: Our privacy practices are built around Canada's federal private-sector privacy law and the provincial health-information legislation that applies wherever we operate. Until the full policy is published, contact our care team with any question about how your information is handled.
legalPages.termsLead: The terms that apply when you use this website.
legalPages.termsBody: Nothing on this website is medical advice, and the information here does not create a care relationship. Service availability differs by province and city, and only the communities listed as active on our locations page are served today.
legalPages.accessibilityLead: What we have done to make this site usable, and how to tell us when it is not.
legalPages.accessibilityIntro: Jarkabi Home Care aims to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA across this website. Accessibility matters more than usual here: many of our visitors are older adults, people with low vision, or families reading on a phone in a hospital corridor.
accessibilityDone: Text and interface colours are checked against the WCAG AA contrast minimums of 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text.
Every page can be operated with a keyboard alone, and focused elements show a visible outline.
Headings follow a single logical order, form fields have visible labels, and images that carry meaning have alternative text.
Interactive targets are at least 24 by 24 pixels, and the layout reflows without horizontal scrolling down to a 320 pixel viewport.
The site is published in seven languages, with right-to-left layout support for Arabic.
accessibilityGaps: Translations outside English and French are partial; untranslated text falls back to English rather than showing an empty page.
Documents published by third parties, such as external forms, may not meet the same standard.
legalPages.accessibilityContactBody: If any part of this site prevents you from finding or requesting care, email our care team and tell us what happened. We treat access barriers as service failures and respond to them the same way.
